# Creating a command

Commands are declared with `defineCommand`, `defineOption` and `defineArgument`, on top of `cliparse`. Options and arguments are validated and parsed by [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas, and their types flow into the handler. The reasons behind this design are explained in [ADR 0001](../adr/adr-0001-rework-file-structure.md).

Before writing a command, look at a similar one and copy its naming, file layout, output format and error messages. `src/commands/drain/` is a good example of a command group with shared arguments and options.

## Example

A fictional `clever coffee brew <blend>` subcommand, part of a `coffee` group (neither exists in the CLI). The `<blend>` argument is shared by several `coffee` subcommands, so it lives in `coffee.args.js`:

```js
// src/commands/coffee/coffee.args.js
import { z } from 'zod';
import { defineArgument } from '../../lib/define-argument.js';

export const blendArg = defineArgument({
  schema: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, 'Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes'),
  description: 'Blend of coffee',
  placeholder: 'blend',
});
```

`--shots`, `--milk` and `--topping` are only used by this subcommand, so they are defined inline. `--format` comes from `global.options.js`:

```js
// src/commands/coffee/coffee.brew.command.js
import { z } from 'zod';
import { brewCoffee } from '../../clever-client/coffee.js';
import { defineCommand } from '../../lib/define-command.js';
import { defineOption } from '../../lib/define-option.js';
import { Logger } from '../../logger.js';
import { sendToApi } from '../../models/send-to-api.js';
import { humanJsonOutputFormatOption } from '../global.options.js';
import { blendArg } from './coffee.args.js';

export const coffeeBrewCommand = defineCommand({
  description: 'Brew a coffee',
  since: null,
  options: {
    shots: defineOption({
      name: 'shots',
      schema: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(1),
      description: 'Number of espresso shots',
      aliases: ['s'],
      placeholder: 'shots',
    }),
    milk: defineOption({
      name: 'milk',
      schema: z.enum(['none', 'whole', 'oat']).default('none'),
      description: 'Kind of milk',
      placeholder: 'milk',
    }),
    toppings: defineOption({
      name: 'topping',
      schema: z
        .union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])
        .transform((value) => (typeof value === 'string' ? [value] : value))
        .optional(),
      description: 'Topping to add. Multiple --topping can be passed',

I haven't added `clever instances` yet. The write that creates `src/commands/instances/instances.command.js` was denied. I undid my one other edit, which registered the command in `src/commands/global.commands.js`, because without the new file that import would break the CLI. The working tree is clean again.

If you allow writes under `src/commands/instances/`, this is what I'll do:

- **Command:** a new `src/commands/instances/instances.command.js` with `since: null`. It takes `--alias`, `--app` and `--format` from `global.options.js` and finds the app with `Application.resolveId`, like `status` does.
- **Data:** it reuses `listInstances` from `src/models/instances.js`, the same call `clever ssh` makes, so no new API code is needed. It lists only running instances, and orders them like `ssh` does: build VMs last, then by instance number, newest first.
- **Human output:** a table with the columns NUMBER (or `build`), ID, NAME, STATE, FLAVOR and CREATION DATE. It uses `formatTable` and `Logger.println`, like `database backups`. With no instance running, it prints "No running instances found for this application".
- **JSON output:** `--format json` prints the list through `Logger.printJson`.
- **Then:** add `instances: instancesCommand` to `global.commands.js`, add a `clever instances` line to `skills/clever-tools/SKILL.md`, and run `npm run docs` and `npm run validate`. I'll also try `node bin/clever.js instances` on an app you name, since it's read-only.

Decision for you: I planned to show running instances only, because without that filter the API also returns old, deleted ones. If you want those too, I can add an `--all` flag.
